text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites, and articles. This training data helps them answer questions, write stories, or translate languages. To get good results, users often practise prompt engineering—writing clear instructions to guide the model. However, LLMs have limits. They can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce biased answers because their knowledge comes from the data they were trained on. They are powerful tools, but they cannot replace human judgement.
